slot.brief: Give E°cell (and n) for a reaction and compute ΔG°; alternatively use ΔG° = −nFE° = −RT ln K to find the equilibrium constant sign or magnitude for the given cell.

stem: At $298\ \text{K}$, a cell reaction transfers $2$ mol of electrons and has $E^\circ_\text{cell}=+0.0592\ \text{V}$. Find its equilibrium constant $K$. Take $2.303RT/F=0.0592\ \text{V}$.
working:
$\log_{10}K=\dfrac{nFE^\circ_\text{cell}}{2.303RT}=\dfrac{2(0.0592)}{0.0592}=2$; hence $K=10^2=100$.

Independent check: At equilibrium, \(\log_{10}K=\frac{nE^\circ}{2.303RT/F}=\frac{2(0.0592)}{0.0592}=2\), so \(K=10^2=100\).

draft.distractor_notes: A: Uses the reciprocal of the correct value. B: Uses the reciprocal and omits the electron-transfer factor of 2. C: Omits the electron-transfer factor of 2.
